entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Iwo Jima, fought from February 19 to March 26, 1945, was a pivotal event in the Pacific Theater of World War II, in which the United States Marine Corps launched an amphibious assault on the Japanese-held island of Iwo Jima. 

 This five-week battle, which resulted in the deaths of over 26,500 Japanese and 26,500 American servicemen, marked a turning point in the war, as it provided the Allies with a crucial airbase and allowed them to launch strategic bombing raids on mainland Japan. 

 The battle's significance extends beyond its immediate impact, as it paved the way for the eventual Allied victory in the Pacific and cemented the United States' position as a global military superpower. 

 The iconic image of the U.S. flag being raised on Iwo Jima's Mount Suribachi, captured by Associated Press photographer Joe Rosenthal, has become an enduring symbol of American determination and sacrifice.
